subject: Coverage for accelerated usage renewal
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@kinetica.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Coverage for accelerated usage renewal

Hi Tom —

Thanks for the heads-up on the Q4 ramp. I pulled together three compact structures that typically work for customers who need predictable economics but want headroom for bursts:

- Option A — Firm uplift: fixed committed units for the remainder of the year, with a stepped discount for increments >30%. Predictable invoice but less flexible.
- Option B — Surge coverage (preferred): a voucher-style "insurance" pool you can draw from for temporary spikes; lower up-front commit and a small premium on drawn units.
- Option C — Consumption floor + overage: lower monthly base (consumption), with an agreed floor and blended overage rate above floor.

I attached a simple pricing worksheet with ballpark numbers and one example that co-terms the uplift to Kinetica's March renewal. Can you confirm which structure your finance team prefers? If you want, we can run quick modeled scenarios off the forecast you mentioned.

Next steps I suggest: you tell us preferred structure, we send a formal quote + SLA carve for surge coverage, then 1x sign-off call.

Cheers,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: Kinetica_pricing_options_v1.xlsx)

From: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@kinetica.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@kinetica.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Coverage for accelerated usage renewal

Hey Stephanie —

Appreciate the options. Quick context from our side: CFO wants minimal variance to forecast for Q4 but we expect a product-led spike the week after Black Friday. Procurement copied — they need an example invoice path and an explicit commitment ceiling.

A couple of asks:
1) Can you show an Option B example where surge insurance is a prepaid credit pool (drawn credits billed at a fixed blended rate) vs a pure voucher?
2) If we co-term to March, can the pool live as a standalone line item (so our accounting treats it as a contract asset)?
3) Any ability to cap downside (i.e., unused credits refunded or converted to discounted reserved units)?

Attached our usage forecast (simple CSV) so you can plug it in. If you can send a short quote grid by EOD Wednesday we can accelerate approvals.

—Tom
(Attachment: Kinetica_usage_forecast.csv)

Folks —

Looping you both to get pricing/legal inputs. Tom asked for an Option B variant where surge insurance acts as a prepaid credit pool that can be drawn down at a fixed blended rate; they also want the pool to be a standalone line item on the contract if we co-term to March. Procurement asked about refund/convertibility of unused credits.

Key constraints: customer needs minimal P&L variance for Q4; they prefer a modest upfront fee rather than a large firm commit.

Can we draft:
- Pricing sheet with 2 x voucher/pool variants (non-refundable vs convertible to reserved units at 60% of list)
- One-line SLA carve for surge availability (priority queue): description + latency SLA exception
- Short paragraph we can include for accounting treatment (how the pool appears on invoice).

I attached our working sheet — please edit.

Thanks,
Steph

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@kinetica.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Coverage for accelerated usage renewal

Steph —

Nice concise brief. I ran numbers off their forecast and propose the following two-priced structures for commercial review:

- Plan B1 (Prepaid credit pool — non-refundable): Prepay $X for a pool that draws at 0.0125 per unit (blended). Upfront fee ~3.5% of estimated 3-month draw to cover runway. No refunds, but unused credits roll into a reduced-rate voucher for next quarter (one-time conversion).

- Plan B2 (Prepaid credit pool — convertible): Prepay $Y, draw at 0.0135 per unit. Unused credits convertible at 60% of list to reserved units with 30-day notice. This shifts some risk back to Redwood but helps procurement.

Discounting: given their growth trajectory, I recommend a 7% volume discount on committed reserved units if they convert >50% of credits within 90 days.

I attached a priced worksheet with line-item math (ballpark). If Legal accepts the convertible clause we can push B2 as the recommended option — it's more palatable to customers and preserves upside.

—Ben
(Attachment: Kinetica_pricing_options_v1.xlsx)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@kinetica.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 12:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Coverage for accelerated usage renewal — legal/ops notes

Thanks team — quick legal/ops flags before we send to the customer:

- SLA carve: acceptable but must be explicit that priority routing for insured draws is subject to capacity; include a fallback model.
- Refunds: Legal prefers conversion over refunds. If we allow refunds, limit to a capped percent (<=25%) and require notice window.
- Accounting/Co-term: If they want the pool as a standalone line item we need to treat it as deferred revenue; require a billing schedule and clear draw reconciliation cadence (monthly).
- Exec approval: Anything that expands SLA or gives refunds needs a credit reserve sign-off from Sales Ops (Marissa), so cc'd.

I'm attaching a short SLA exception draft and a redline we can send. Recommend we propose Plan B2 (convertible) + a 60-day conversion window, with monthly reconciliation and a 10% capped refundable allowance only on the first draw period.

—Lauren
Legal Ops 
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: SLA-exception-request.pdf)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Subject: Final: proposed path forward for surge coverage (summary)

Tom —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and for sharing the forecast. Per our internal review, here's the recommended path we can put on a formal quote today:

1) Recommended: Plan B2 — Prepaid convertible pool (co-term to 2027-03-31).
   - Upfront: $Y (invoiceable as a separate line item, appears as deferred revenue)
   - Draw rate: $0.0135 per unit (blended) when used
   - Conversion: unused credits convertible to reserved units at 60% of list within 60 days after quarter close
   - Refunds: limited refundable allowance 10% of pool value for first draw period only

2) SLA carve: priority routing for insured draws; documented fallback if capacity constraints exist (no availability credits promised beyond standard SLA).

3) Next steps: I can send a clean quote + the SLA exception redline and the DocuSign packet. If that looks good, we'll aim for signature by next Tue (2026-10-19) to ensure provisioning before the anticipated Black Friday spike.
